obligations.description: Provide a definition for the forward-difference approximation for f : ℝ → ℝ at real x with real step h, exactly (f (x+h) - f x) / h.

State the theorem for arbitrary f D : ℝ → ℝ and x h L : ℝ, assuming 0 < h, 0 ≤ L, ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc x (x+h)), ∀ t ∈ Set.Ioo x (x+h), HasDerivAt f (D t) t, and ∀ t ∈ Set.Ioo x (x+h), |D t - D x| ≤ L * |t-x|. Conclude |forwardDifference f x h - D x| ≤ L*h. Preserve D x as the given reference value without adding endpoint derivative assumptions.
Establish x < x+h from 0 < h, and simplify (x+h)-x to h. Positivity also ensures the step is nonzero if explicit division manipulations are used.

Apply exists_hasDerivAt_eq_slope to f, D, endpoints x and x+h, the closed-interval continuity hypothesis, and the open-interval HasDerivAt hypothesis. Obtain c ∈ Set.Ioo x (x+h) with D c = (f (x+h)-f x)/((x+h)-x). Simplify the denominator to identify D c with the defined forward difference. This interior witness is the required construction linking the derivative variation hypothesis to the finite difference.
Extract x < c and c < x+h from the witness membership. Deduce 0 ≤ c-x and c-x ≤ h, hence |c-x| ≤ h by abs_of_nonneg and real linear arithmetic.

Specialize the original variation bound at the same interior witness. Use mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left with 0 ≤ L to get L*|c-x| ≤ L*h, and combine the inequalities. Rewrite the witness equality and unfold the forward-difference definition to obtain the stated error bound, keeping the subtraction order D c - D x consistent.
